Charge control needs support from your device’s ROM, and a permission that apps cannot grant themselves. You set it up by hand.

Currently: Pixel 6a or newer phones on Android 15+, Samsung on verified One UI versions, Xiaomi on HyperOS 2, and OnePlus, Oppo, or Realme on ColorOS 15. Amply checks your exact device and shows what works.
You grant the permission yourself: with one ADB command from a computer, or through the Shizuku app. Some devices require Shizuku. The dashboard walks you through the right option.

Amply needs one durable Android permission to change the charge policy.

With Shizuku, Amply can confirm the configured policy and run diagnostics, not just write it. Start or install Shizuku and allow Amply; the durable permission is then granted automatically. The button below is a manual fallback if that fails.
Easiest: no ADB install needed. On the computer your phone is plugged into, open this link in Chrome or Edge to grant control over USB. Shizuku is still needed for diagnostics and reliable readback.
Or, if you already have ADB set up on that computer, run:
Amply detects the permission automatically once it runs, or tap Refresh in the top bar.
This guide reads your hidden settings through Shizuku (read-only). Install and start Shizuku, then come back.
Help add support for your device
You\'ll switch your phone\'s battery-protection setting a few times while Amply records which hidden settings change. Nothing is sent until you review it and choose what to include.
This produces candidate information to help a maintainer. It does not enable control on your device.
Both answers below are needed. Even if the capture finds nothing, they tell a maintainer which software your phone runs and what to look for.
What is it called on your phone? e.g. \"Protect battery\", \"Battery care\"
From Settings › About phone, e.g. \"One UI 8\", \"HyperOS 2\", \"ColorOS 15\"
Don\'t enter serial numbers, IMEI, or account names. This goes into a public report.

Known charging settings are included automatically. Everything else is hidden: reveal a row to inspect it on your device, then choose whether to include it.
Nothing changed in the secure, global, or system settings between the modes you captured. That usually means one of:

• The mode wasn\'t actually switched in the system settings between captures.\n• It was switched, but captured before the system applied it. Wait until the manufacturer\'s screen shows the new mode, then capture.\n• This ROM keeps the mode somewhere Amply can\'t read.

There\'s nothing to send from this run, so this is as far as it goes. Start over and capture each mode again if you think one of the first two applies. If your phone has no battery-protection setting to switch, or it keeps it somewhere Amply can\'t read, then this device can\'t be mapped this way.

Settings did change, but none are in the report yet. Support for a new device is usually hiding behind one of the rows below, so reveal them, check that nothing personal is in there, and include at least one. A report with no settings can\'t be used.

Your build accepts a charge limit, but whether the charging hardware actually honours it differs from build to build, so Amply can\'t offer the controls yet. Run a check on this device: Amply watches one charge and switches the controls on only if the battery really stops at the limit.

The controls are available, but nothing here proves the limit yet. Set a limit, then charge from below it and leave the charger connected: Amply confirms once the battery is observed holding at the limit, and switches the controls back off if it charges past it.

Your build accepted the limit and then charged past it, so the charging hardware is ignoring it. Amply has switched its charging controls off here rather than show a protection that isn\'t real. A report helps get this build looked at.

At the 80% limit, unplug for at least 2 seconds and reconnect within 10. An ongoing notification keeps the gesture reliable.

Optionally use a quick unplug/replug at the 80% limit to charge fully once.
Watch for a quick unplug and reconnect that starts a one-time full charge. Keeps an ongoing notification while it watches.
Arm the gesture whenever a protective policy is detected, not just while the 80% limit is holding the battery.
More sensitive: any unplug/replug of 2–10 seconds starts a full charge, e.g. also below 80%. Momentary power cuts shorter than 2 seconds, like a car cutting USB power while starting, never trigger.

Samsung phones include battery protection under Settings → Battery → Battery protection. Amply can\'t control it directly on this device, but you can turn it on there.
OnePlus and Oppo phones offer charge limiting under Settings → Battery → Battery health (or Smart charging). Amply can\'t control it directly on this device, but you can enable it there.
Xiaomi, Redmi, and POCO phones may offer charge limiting or protection under Settings → Battery → Battery protection. Amply can\'t control it directly on this device, but you can look for it there.
Look for charging optimization under Settings → Battery. Amply can\'t control it directly on this device.
LineageOS includes Charging control under Settings → Battery. Amply can\'t control it directly on this device, but you can set a limit there.
Your phone may offer a built-in battery-protection or charge-limit option in its battery settings. Amply can\'t control it directly on this device, but it\'s worth a look.
